title: peak-lens-sidecar — the Scanalyzer's downloaded .PEAK
description: The artifact written by `exportPeakSidecar` in `SAMPLE and PLAY/libControl/MusicChart/LensesView.jsx` and downloaded by a person as `<name>.PEAK`. THE EXTENSION `.PEAK` NAMES FOUR DOCUMENTS IN THIS REPOSITORY AND THIS IS ONE OF THEM; the other three are the analyzer's per-file sidecar, the analyzer's aggregate `sample_cloud_data.PEAK` (an ARRAY of exactly those, which is what peakSchema.ts beside this file reads), and `extract_note_root_beat_map.py`'s partial write — all three typed by `analyzerPeakSchema.json` beside this file since PLAN-907.01, and enumerated in its `$comment`. Nothing in the extension distinguishes any of them, so the `format` field does; it exists for exactly the reason the sibling .PERF's does. THIS SCHEMA TYPES WHAT THE EXPORT WRITES, AND UNTIL PLAN-1067.02 NOTHING TYPED WHAT THE IMPORT READS: `handleImportFile`'s whole gate was `if (parsed.musicality || parsed.beat_markers)`, which the analyzer's per-file .PEAK passes, so it imported and reported success. `identifyPeakDocument` in that same file is now the read-side counterpart of this document — it branches on `format` and `metadata.analyzer_version` and on nothing else, and it is where the version policy is written down: an unknown MAJOR refuses, an unknown MINOR imports, and a version-less file predates 1.0.0 and is still read on its keys.
$comment: IT SHIPPED WITH NO VERSION AT ALL, WHICH IS THE OMISSION peakSchema.ts IS AN ACCOUNT OF. That file is 115 lines of migration for a format that changed shape and broke its reader, and its own header argues that two fields would have prevented it — while the export beside it went on writing neither. `format` and `schema_version` are those two fields. Written off four real exports driven through test/harness.mjs, not off a reading of the source, and held by .apk.scripts/check_lens_exports.py: `additionalProperties: false` with a complete `required` list is what turns a renamed key into a red lane instead of a silent shape change. 1.1.0 SNAKE_CASED THE NINE KEYS INSIDE `musicality` AND `loudness_ebu_r128`, WHICH WERE THE ONLY camelCase IN THE DOCUMENT. They carried the scan's in-memory spelling because those two objects were handed through verbatim from oaScanMeasure.js; `exportPeakSidecar` now maps them through one table per group, and `handleImportFile` reads BOTH spellings off that same table so a 1.0.0 file a visitor already downloaded still imports — a version bump with no migration is exactly the omission peakSchema.ts is 115 lines of aftermath from (PLAN-1067.01). THE ANALYZER'S NAMES WERE NOT ADOPTED: its `musicality` says root_note_name/root_frequency_hz/beats_per_minute for three of these measurements, and taking those would have made one app write `key` in the .PERF.json and `root_note_name` in the .PEAK it downloads beside it. The vocabulary chosen is the one lensPerfExportSchema.json beside this file has pinned since PLAN-802.01. TWO GROUP NAMES COLLIDE WITH THE ANALYZER'S FORMAT AND SHARE EXACTLY ONE FIELD: `musicality` is {key, key_confidence, pitch_hz, cents_offset, bpm} here and {pitch_hz, root_note_name, root_frequency_hz, root_cents_offset, beats_per_minute, root_midi_note, chromagram, ...} there; `ucs` is {cat_key, creator_id, source_id} here and {category, subcategory, id, confidence, alternatives, synonyms, reason} there. A reader that branches on a group NAME therefore reads the wrong document and gets plausible numbers with no error, which is why `format` and `metadata.analyzer_version` are the only two things anything may branch on. The one shared name is `musicality.pitch_hz`, it is the same measurement on both sides, and `.apk.scripts/check_peak_formats.py` holds the overlap at EXACTLY that one field — an allowlist, so a second accidental share is still a red lane. `ucs` remains disjoint.

format.description: The discriminator between this and the analyzer's .PEAK. The analyzer's carries no `format` and does carry `metadata.analyzer_version`; a reader that finds neither is holding something older than both.

schema_version.description: Semver, and a `const` so a bump must move this file with it. 1.0.0 was the first version this format ever announced; every file written before it is version-less and identifiable only by its keys. 1.1.0 snake_cased the nine keys inside `musicality` and `loudness_ebu_r128` (PLAN-1067.01), and `handleImportFile` reads a 1.0.0 file's camelCase as well as this one's — the version is how a READER of a file, which cannot see the exporter, tells which spelling to look for. 1.2.0 MADE FOUR FIELDS NULLABLE: `bext_time_reference` and the three `spatial_aes69` numbers, which were constants standing in for measurements nothing takes (PLAN-908.01). A MINOR on purpose — no key was renamed and none was removed — so every 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 file already on a visitor's disk still imports: `identifyPeakDocument` refuses an unknown MAJOR only.

filename.description: The source audio's name as the page received it, container extension and all.

ucs.description: Universal Category System identity, as typed into the taxonomy lens. Strings the operator owns; the schema does not judge them.

musicality.description: Mapped out of the scan's in-memory shape through `PEAK_MUSICALITY_KEYS`, not handed through verbatim — which is what it was until 1.1.0, and why these five keys were camelCase in a snake_case document. null only if a scan somehow carried none; every key inside is present with a null value when unmeasurable.

key.description: The Krumhansl-Schmuckler winner, e.g. `C Major`. NOT the analyzer's `root_note_name`, which is a pitch class and not a key.

key_confidence.description: Pearson correlation against the best-matching Krumhansl-Schmuckler profile. `keyConfidence` before 1.1.0, and the analyzer's format has no counterpart for it at all.

pitch_hz.description: THE ONE FIELD NAME THIS FORMAT SHARES WITH THE ANALYZER'S, and it is the same measurement on both sides: the detected fundamental in Hz. `pitchHz` before 1.1.0. check_peak_formats.py holds the overlap between the two `musicality` groups at exactly this.

cents_offset.description: Cents from the nearest equal-tempered note. `centsOffset` before 1.1.0; the analyzer spells its own as `root_cents_offset`, so the two do not collide.

bpm.description: The analyzer spells its own `beats_per_minute`. Unchanged in 1.1.0 — it was never camelCase.

beat_markers.description: Onsets in file order. Empty, never absent — it was `undefined` and therefore dropped by JSON.stringify until PLAN-601.01, which is how a broken sidecar came to look like a complete one.

loudness_ebu_r128.description: EBU R128 / ITU-R BS.1770-4 figures, mapped through `PEAK_LOUDNESS_KEYS` rather than handed through verbatim — which is what they were until 1.1.0, and why these four keys were camelCase. These are the same four measurements the `.PERF.json` beside this file has always written as integrated_lufs / max_true_peak_dbtp / lra_lu / gating_threshold_lufs; now they agree. An unmeasurable one is null: -70 LUFS is 'too quiet to measure' and 0 LUFS is the loudest number in the unit.

archival_aes.description: The preservation block. Its checksum is of the DECODED SAMPLES and says so — the constant that stood here was the SHA-256 of the empty string, printed under an archival heading (PLAN-601.01).

pcm_sha256.description: null on an insecure origin, where WebCrypto is not there to ask.

bext_time_reference.description: BWF bext timeReference, `null` and NOT `0`. A 0 here is not 'unknown' — it is the claim that this audio begins at sample zero of the timeline it was recorded against, and only the `bext` chunk carries that. The page holds a decoded AudioBuffer; the chunk did not survive the decode. Same block, same correction and the same `null` as the empty-string SHA-256 that stood in `pcm_sha256` (PLAN-601.01, PLAN-908.01).

spatial_aes69.description: AES69 SOFA placement, and NOTHING IN THIS VIEW MEASURES ONE. The three numbers were `0.0, 0.0, 1.0`, which reads off the file as 'the source is dead ahead at one metre': no control offers a placement, no scan derives one, no importer fills one in, and `grep -n azimuth_deg` finds a single site in the component — the literal. They are `null` until something measures them, and the day one becomes real this file has to move with it. `sofa_format` stays a `const` because it is a different kind of statement: it names the vocabulary the numbers would be expressed in, the way `sha256_scope` names the scope of a `pcm_sha256` that is usually null. PLAN-908.01.

lyrics.description: Lines a PERSON put in, normalised on the way out so the key is never absent and never an array. Called lyrics_vad until PLAN-629.01, which is a name that claimed Voice Activity Detection over a scanner that runs none.

vadSegments.description: Present only on the dictation and .LRC-import path, where it is written empty. Optional for that reason, and holding the name PLAN-629.01 left in place inside the object rather than on it.
